derivations.note: ⭐ Per feedback_physics-first-worldengine-scoping and the charter's INTENT FRAME, these are DECISIONS MADE, not questions pending. Each is derived from the code or from published physics and is stated here so Max can overrule any of them at greenlight rather than be interviewed about them.
derivations.D1_two_fields_not_one: THE FIX IS A FIELD SPLIT, AND THIS IS FORCED, NOT PREFERRED. MoonGenerator.js:265 computes `moon.massEarth = radiusEarth**3 * (composition.density / RHO_EARTH_KGM3)` and PhysicsEngine's density is a harmonic-mean ice/rock VOLUME mixture of `volatileFraction`. Raising Earth's volatileFraction from ≤0.06 to 0.15 as ONE field drops an Earth analogue's bulk density from ~4870 to ~3090 kg/m³ — which (a) re-rolls every moon's mass, and through checkTidalLock every moon's `locked` flag, which the relief dispatch tests FIRST, and (b) pushes Earth analogues under surfaceMaterial.js's DENS_ROCK_LO 3.5 g/cc so they start reading partly ICY. So `deriveComposition` must return TWO fields: `iceFraction` (accreted bulk ice — the existing frost-ratio law, kept verbatim, and the ONLY input to density and to the ice-rock surfaceType test) and `volatileFraction` (surface volatile inventory — the new law).
derivations.D2_reconciliation_direction: THE GENERATOR MOVES TO THE ENGINE'S SCALE, NOT THE REVERSE. The REPORT left this open. It is settled by which side is anchored. The engine's scale is calibrated on SIX real bodies recorded in driver-presets.js — Earth 0.15, Mars 0.10, Venus 0.02, Moon/Mercury 0.02, Titan 0.40, Europa 0.50 — and surfaceMaterial.js:347-367 records a whole re-derivation of the oxidiser window against four of them, INCLUDING an explicitly REFUSED corpus-fitted alternative with the reason written down: 'Fitting the law to our own generator is how a world-generation defect becomes a palette law.' The generator's scale is a piecewise ramp in frostRatio with no reference body on it anywhere. The anchored side wins. ⇒ zero edits under src/worldengine/; the entire change is in src/generation/.
derivations.D3_the_law_shape: SURFACE INVENTORY = (in-situ accreted + delivered) × retained. (i) IN-SITU: the existing frost-ratio term, which is right beyond the frost line and correctly ~0 inside it — this is what keeps Titan and Europa where they are. (ii) DELIVERED: late accretion of volatile-rich planetesimals scattered inward from beyond the frost line; a SYSTEM-level property, weakly dependent on the receiving body's own orbit. Its physical drivers are the system's solid reservoir and its giant-planet architecture, and the giant-planet–metallicity correlation is one of the best-established results in exoplanet science. ⭐ BOTH INPUTS ALREADY EXIST ON `zones`: `metallicity`, and `solidInventory` (StarSystemGenerator.js:467, computed from starMassSolar × formation.solidFraction and marked UNREAD BY DESIGN, plan B3 — this workstream is its reader). (iii) RETAINED: loss governed by T_eq and by escape velocity over age. The five inner-system anchors DERIVE the shape rather than fit it — Mars (0.107 M⊕, 210 K) is wetter than Venus (0.815 M⊕, 737 K), so TEMPERATURE dominates mass in the inner system, which is the runaway-greenhouse / photodissociation loss channel; and Moon/Mercury (~0.03 M⊕) at 0.02 is the Jeans/airless channel. (iv) STOCHASTIC: delivery is a few large impactors, so its variance is large — that variance IS the 'wide variety' Max asked for, and it is what turns a single monotone dial into a distribution.
derivations.D4_no_new_rng_draw: ⛔ THE DELIVERY TERM CONSUMES ZERO NEW DRAWS FROM THE SHARED STREAM. PlanetGenerator.js:364 passes `rng.float()` off the shared planet stream; adding a second draw there shifts every downstream value and silently regenerates the entire galaxy. Any stochastic component comes from a namespaced sub-seed keyed on stable identity — the precedent is in the same file (PlanetGenerator.js `eccSeed`, whose comment states the rule) and in MoonGenerator.js:256 (`mooncomp:`).
derivations.D5_the_locked_gate_is_OUT_of_scope_and_t: The REPORT's Block B — `if (locked) return shell('eyeball-despun')` sitting ABOVE both roads to plate() and eating 74 % of bodies — is NOT in this workstream, and the reason is a measurement taken during scoping (scope-probe.mjs, 200 seeds): of the 11 bodies that are both in the plate band's mass window AND temperate, **6 are UNLOCKED**. So the volatile fix ALONE opens the plate path; Block B is not a hard cap on it. Moving the locked test is a relief-DISPATCH redesign in a different module and belongs to its own workstream. AC-4 measures how many bodies reach plate() so we learn whether Block B is still binding.
derivations.D6_the_rate_is_reported_never_asserted: Earth analogues will stay RARE — 11 of 1,183 bodies are even in the mass+temperate window, so the ceiling is ~1 per 18 systems before wetness is considered. That is the real occurrence rate and Max's ruling ('a simulation of the milky way galaxy') selects it. ⭐ THE HEADLINE IS NOT EARTH TWINS: it is the 135 TEMPERATE BODIES — 11.4 % of all solid bodies, ~6 per system — going from 100 % bone-dry to a distribution.
